texts: After my knee surgery I looked at my body differently, fragile, patched, and dear, and I knew it was something I looked after but was not.
doha about how delicate this body is
Write a verse about the human body being fragile and precious at once, to be cared for and thanked, but never mistaken for the one who lives in it and who will one day leave it.
Nine gates in a frail frame, a borrowed breath for its guest; guard it tenderly, for it will not stay.
fragile body, precious gift
body, borrowed and precious
Compose a doha about this body as a precious gift to be kept healthy for use in service and prayer, yet not clung to or worshipped, since it is only a temporary form given for a short time.
This breathing frame was lent to me for a season; may I treat it with care and not call it mine.
My father kept his body fit until eighty, but he used to say that he was only the tenant of it, and he treated it like a rented room he loved.
doha on this body being temporary but valuable
My uncle, a lifelong traveler, now sits in a chair, his body tested and worn by every road, and he says the touchstone of time has had its say.
traveler, touchstone, worn body
The traveller's body wears out on the road; the touchstone of age tests every limb until the frame gives way.
Write a verse about this body of the traveler, tested by age as metal by the touchstone, wearing a little more each day until it can walk no further, and the traveler who is not this body goes on.
doha on the traveler's body slowly wearing out
body, cherish, not cling
Give me a verse about taking good care of this body, feeding and resting it with love, yet remembering that it is a fragile covering, soon to be set down, and not the true identity of anyone.
Dress the form with gentle care, but do not call it yourself, for it will fade like a promise.
Every morning I stretch my aching back and thank it for another day of carrying me, while knowing I am not it.
doha on loving your body but not being proud of it
A frame of flesh, warmed by a fire that will go out, lodged for a night in an inn that will be sold.
body, fire, inn
Write a doha about this body as an inn in which the soul lodges for a brief while, kept warm by the fire of life, which, when it burns low, leaves the inn cold and empty.
doha on how this body is just a temporary stay, fire inside it too
In the hospital the nurse said that the fire in my father's body was fading, and I thought of it as an inn where a guest was preparing to leave.
moon, moneylender, borrowed body
Compose a verse about this body as a loan from the moneylender of time, who comes at the end of the allotted days and takes it back, as the moon takes back its light with each waning.
doha about the moon and a moneylender and how this body is on loan
Like the moon, this body waxes and wanes; the moneylender will call to take back what he lent.
Looking at the moon over the crowded street, I thought of my body as something the moneylender of the universe had lent me, with a due date unknown.
Our cleric used to climb the stairs to the pulpit with ease, and now he leans on two people and says gently that this body is only a coat.
Write a doha about the cleric whose voice is still strong but whose body is fading as surely as everyone's, reminding us that holiness lives in the heart and this body is just a changing form.
doha about how even a cleric's body grows old
The cleric preaches, yet his body bends and wearies like all others; a robe cannot hide the frailty beneath.
cleric, aging body
thief, moth, fading body
doha on how the thief of age steals this body, a moth to the glow
Write a verse about the thief of age who steals strength, sight, and agility from this body one night at a time, while the moth of youth flies still around the glow, unaware.
The thief of time steals the strength of this body, a moth to the glow of youth, circling and circling.
Every year my body loses a little more, as if a quiet thief were at work, and I recall how I flew about like a moth at twenty.
The fly lands where the warmth has gone; this body was a refuge, no longer, no more.
fly, ageing body
Write a verse about this body that the fly settles on once life has gone, and about the dignity of a form that carried a life and deserves care but cannot be the end of anyone.
At the village clinic I saw a fly circling a very ill man and I felt how thin the line is between the living body and a body at rest.
doha on a body, the fly, and decay
A traveler on our road once told me his body was like a bitter gourd, all green and sturdy outside while the bitterness of age grew within.
Write a doha about how the traveler carries his body as a bitter gourd carries its bitterness, outwardly bright and fresh but spoiling from within, and how it must be treated with care and not trust.
bitter gourd, traveler, body
The traveler leans on this body as on a staff, but the bitter gourd of flesh turns sour with the years.
doha on body as a bitter gourd traveler?
Write a verse about this body carried to its first celebration in a palanquin and to its last rites on a bier, borne on the shoulders of others both times, and about the fragile guest within.
A palanquin carried you at the wedding, a bier at the end; the same body rides both, borne by other men.
doha on the palanquin and the bier, this body's two rides
bier, palanquin, this body's journey
My grandfather rode a palanquin at his wedding, and at his funeral the same village men carried the bier, and I wondered at this body's short journey between.
weaver's loom, body woven
Write a doha about this body being woven by the unseen weaver's loom out of breath, blood, and bone, worn for a few years, and eventually put aside as the cloth is put aside when it grows thin.
Threads of breath are woven on the weaver's loom of the womb, and the cloth, once worn, is laid aside.
doha about this body as woven cloth from the weaver's loom
The weaver at our loom told me that the cloth wears out in the end no matter how fine, and I thought of my own frame.
doha about the moon and my aging body
On the night of the full moon I looked back at my body of twenty years ago and compared it to my body now, and felt it was a waning thing.
Compose a verse about this body that waxes in youth like the moon and wanes in age, a gift of time that we must tend with care but cannot keep, as the sky cannot keep any one phase.
The moon grows full and wanes again; so this body, bright with youth, is slowly lessened by the years.
moon, waning body
Write a doha on this body as a spinning wheel that turns for a few decades and slows, creaks, and stops, having spun the yarn of a life, which is a gift to cherish but cannot be held forever.
The spinning wheel slows, the breath grows shorter, the yarn of this body's days is almost spun.
spinning wheel, tired body
My grandmother's spinning wheel slowed as her health did, and the day it was silent, I saw her body was just as still, and understood the wheel.
doha on this body as a spinning wheel winding down
doha on this body being strong as an elephant but with one door
My uncle was as strong as an elephant, and when the door of his heart closed in one afternoon the whole family realised how fragile the strongest body is.
Write a verse about this body, mighty as an elephant in its prime, yet with doors that can be closed in a moment, for even the strongest frame is a fragile dwelling and will be left.
elephant, door, body's end
The elephant is strong, yet even it falls; the door of this body creaks, then closes, and the guest walks out.
From a small seed the lotus of this body blooms, so fair, so brief; its petals fall and it forgets itself.
Write a doha about this body as a lotus that blooms from a small seed in muddy water, so lovely for a season, then dropping its petals and returning to the seed it came from.
doha on this body, a lotus on a seed of days
lotus, seed, body
Watching a lotus flower bloom and drop its petals from a single seed, I thought of my own body and its short spring.
palace, lock, body
A palace of flesh, locked against the world, yet the breath slips out through a hundred unseen gaps.
Write a verse about a body proud as a palace with a strong lock on its gates, yet death needs no key; and about the modest worth of a body warmed and tended briefly.
doha on this body as a palace with a lock that does not hold
My neighbour spent a fortune keeping his body strong, a palace with the best lock, but when the heart failed no lock was of any use.
bell, needle, body
Compose a verse about this body which is like a bell, sounding for its short time, and about time, the needle that stitches the hours together, as each ring fades into silence.
The bell of this body rings out its hours, and the needle of time stitches them shut one by one.
doha on this body: a bell and a needle
Every time the clock bell rings I feel my body ageing a little, as though a needle were stitching the days closed.
The heron stands on the river's bank, still and thin, and so we stand on the bank of this body, watching it flow.
Write a doha on this body as a bank beside the river of time, where the heron stands for a moment, and about the guest who stands there only for a while before wading into the current.
heron, river, passing body
By the river, watching a thin heron stand on one leg, I thought of how fragile my own frame is, a bank soon to be washed away.
doha on this body as a river bank and the heron
A beggar dozing at my gate looked exactly as frail and human as my rich father on his sickbed, and the salt on both their skin was the same.
Compose a verse about the beggar and the king who have the same body, made of the same stuff, fed by the same salt, falling to the same fate, and about the worth of a human form regardless of rank.
Beggar or king, this body is the same salt of the earth, and the same dust receives it back.
beggar, salt, same body
doha on the beggar's body and this body of a king, salt
doha on respecting my body without worshipping it
I started eating sensibly and walking every day to honour my body, yet I keep reminding myself that this is only the temporary loan I live in.
Write a doha about this body with its nine gates, every one of them a channel of the world, a gift to be respected and cared for, but not to be confused with who lives behind them.
nine gates of this body
This frame of breath and blood, this frame of nine openings, is wondrous and brief; tend it gently, but do not take it for yourself.
Drawn in sand, this body's outline fades with the first wave, and the fly settles where the warmth has been.
fly, sand, mortal body
Write a verse about this body as a figure drawn in sand, gone with the next wave, and the fly that settles on it when the warmth leaves, and about the dignity of a form that was only lent.
As children we drew ourselves in the sand and watched the tide erase us, and I never understood until the day I saw the fly on my grandfather's still face.
doha on a fly and sand, this body fading
My mother folded my father's cotton shirts after the funeral and said this body was only the shirt, but she touched it with as much love.
Wrap this body in cotton or silk, it is no more than a brief covering; honour it, and let it go.
cotton, body as clothing
doha about this body as cotton clothing for the soul
Compose a doha about this body as a garment of soft cotton worn by the living one for a little while, to be washed, mended, and honoured, and then folded away gently when the wearing is done.
A little cold and the strongest frame lies down; how frail a thing is this breathing garment.
fragile, grateful for health
Write a verse about the way a single fever or fall can remind us how fragile this body is, how much we take it for granted, and how it deserves our gratitude on every ordinary day we are healthy.
After one week of flu I looked at my healthy self a week earlier and wished I had been more thankful for every easy breath.
doha on how fragile this body is to illness
fly, body, temporary
A fly rests on this body's hand; one day neither will move, and the earth will take both back.
Compose a doha about this body that is a loan to life for a few decades only, whose warmth attracts the fly and whose stillness the fly forgets, and about caring for it while it is ours.
doha on this body being temporary, with a fly
A fly sat on my sleeping grandfather's hand and he did not shoo it, and I understood how fragile and quiet a body becomes.
cotton, date palm, body
My father, tall as a date palm in his youth, now wears loose cotton clothes that hang from his frame, and he laughs at the passing of seasons.
doha on cotton clothes and the date palm of this body
This body is a tall date palm, sweet and high, and the cotton dressing it wears away with a few seasons.
Write a verse about this body standing tall like a date palm, bearing sweetness in its prime, and the cotton clothes with which we decorate it, both to be loved and both to be eventually let go.
traveler, elephant, body
doha on the traveler and the elephant, this body
A traveler once told me that he thanked his body every night for carrying him that day, as one thanks an elephant at the journey's end.

Compose a doha on this body that carries the traveler through life like an elephant carries a rider, strong and patient, yet worn by the journey, and to be thanked at the end rather than mistaken for the rider.
The traveler rides the elephant of his body across a long road, and dismounts at the last gate with thanks.
doha about this body as a churn, worn out by use
My mother's hands, worn from years at the churn, taught me that this body is a servant to be thanked and not a master to be served.

Write a doha on this body that works like a churn, day after day, turning the food of life into energy and thought, and which wears slowly until it must be set down, deserving gratitude for its labour.
churn, body, tender care
Like the churn that is worn smooth by use, this body is worn by years of service; honour its wear.
This body is a temple of breath, to be swept and honoured; yet the temple is not the Lord.
doha about this body being a temple but not the god
My teacher told me that I should look after my body as one tends a temple, but remember that I am the worshipper and not the building.
Compose a verse about this body as a temple to be kept clean and cared for, but never mistaken for the god who dwells within it, since the stones of the temple crumble but the dweller does not.
body, temple, not the god
rare human body
doha about this body: precious but fading
Write a verse about the rare gift of a human body, with its senses and breath, which should not be wasted in idleness, but also never be confused with the one who is lent it for a short season.
I turned forty last week and for the first time I felt thankful for each tired limb, and clear that none of it was truly mine to keep.
Rare is this human frame, rarer still the wisdom to use it wisely before it fades.
swan, beggar, body left behind
A beggar and a prince died the same winter in our town, and both bodies were laid down the same way as the swans flew south.
The swan departs the lake and leaves the pond still; so the beggar and the king alike leave their bodies behind.
Write a doha on the swan that leaves the lake and the guest that leaves this body, rich or beggar, each departing with the same simplicity and leaving behind a form that was only borrowed.
doha on the swan leaving this body behind, beggar too
moth, cloud, brief body
doha on the moth and the cloud, the short life of this body
The moth's body is a cloud of dust by morning, and the cloud's body is gone by noon; so is ours.
Compose a doha about this body as brief as a moth's life and as shifting as a cloud, lovely for a moment, and about caring tenderly for such a short-lived thing without grasping it.
Watching a moth die at the window while a cloud passed over, I felt how short the stay of any body is, mine included.
gold, sandalwood, body
Write a verse about this body, which no amount of gold can preserve and no sandalwood can perfume forever, and about the honest care that is due to it as a gift that must still be returned.
My aunt spends hours on sandalwood paste and gold jewellery for her body, and I wish someone would tell her gently that it is not the point.
Anoint it with sandalwood, deck it with gold; this body, adorned or bare, goes the same way.
doha on gold and sandalwood, but this body is neither
Each breath is a coin lent by the moneylender, and this body is the pledge he will reclaim.
Compose a doha about the moneylender who keeps accounts of every borrowed breath and one day arrives to take back this body he lent, which can be neither bargained with nor refused.
doha on the moneylender who wants this body
moneylender, body, borrowed
My uncle always said his body was a loan from a moneylender he had never met, and at the end he repaid the debt with a smile.
I saw myself in the mirror after the funeral and thought of the shroud, how the same body had to be dressed so differently on two occasions.
Write a doha about the mirror that shows this body at its best and the shroud that waits for it at the end, and about caring for the form without confusing it with the one who looks.
doha on the mirror, shroud, and this body
mirror, shroud, body
Face the mirror and see a shroud-bound shape, a form on loan, fair now, folded away by evening.
At the end of autumn I watched a last leaf cling to a branch and a chakor bird in the distance, and thought of my father's slow dying.
doha on the chakor bird, a leaf, this body
chakor bird, leaf, body
The chakor bird longs for what is far, a leaf trembles on its twig; this body trembles, too, awaiting its fall.
Compose a doha about this body as a leaf trembling on its twig in autumn, and the chakor bird that longs for something far away, hanging by a thin stem on what we most love.
doha on the shroud, prayer beads, and body
shroud, prayer beads, body
Write a verse about this body that holds prayer beads in its fingers and will one day be wrapped in a shroud, and about the days between, when it is a gift for devotion, not a possession.
My grandmother keeps her prayer beads in one hand and her folded shroud on the shelf, and says her body is just the in-between.
The beads turn, the shroud waits folded, and this body between them is lent just long enough for prayer.
doha on the thief that steals our body bit by bit
No guard can keep the thief from this frame of breath; he takes a little each year, and the frame grows light.
I keep losing small things, my sight, my hearing, my speed, as if a quiet thief were visiting my body each night.
thief, body, hidden loss
Compose a verse about the thief who creeps into this body year after year, taking strength, sight, and hearing, and about caring for what is left with tenderness, since it can never be fully guarded.
bitter gourd, body, outward show
doha on a bitter gourd body, nice outside
My cousin spends hours at the gym for a body that will look perfect, but my aunt, who cooks bitter gourd, says the outside never tells you what ripens within.
The bitter gourd outside is green and plump, this body outside is fair and strong; both know the bitterness within time.
Write a doha on this body that looks smooth and fresh like a bitter gourd, but which hides the slow turning of years inside, to be cared for tenderly and not trusted to last.
Weary servant, faithful frame, I thank you; one day I will lay you down, but not yet, not today.
doha on feeling disconnected from my aching body
aching body, thank it
When my back hurt all week, I realised I had never once thanked it for all the years of quietly working.
Give me a verse about this body that aches and tires and yet is still owed kindness, since it is a faithful servant that carries us without complaint through each day until its work is done.
lotus, body, brief bloom
The lotus of this body opens at dawn and closes by dusk, and the muddy pond remembers nothing of its beauty.
Looking at an old photo of my young self, I thought of how the lotus flowers in our pond bloom for only a few days.
doha on this body as a lotus, brief and lovely
Compose a verse about this body as a lotus whose beauty lasts a single season, a thing to be admired and cared for in its bloom, and gently let go when the petals fall away.
Write a verse about this body as a temporary dwelling with nine gates, kept swept and welcoming for its tenant, but understood to be a rented space that will be handed back.
Nine gates open on the world, and by them the breath comes and goes; soon the last will close.
body, nine gates
honestly just a doha about this body as a temporary dwelling place
While cleaning my flat before moving out, I thought of how my body is the same, a place I keep tidy and will leave soon.
The tortoise carries its shell, the soldier his sword; this body is a shell, and the sword of time cuts it all the same.
tortoise, sword, body shell
A tortoise in our courtyard has outlived two generations of the family, and my grandfather, a sword-swinging soldier in his youth, said this body outlasts nothing.

Compose a doha about this body as a shell like the tortoise's, which protects and carries us but cannot defend against the sword of time, and about the gentle respect due to something so briefly useful.
doha on the tortoise and the sword and this body shell
cage, breath, body
Write a verse about this body as a cage in which the breath sings for a few years before it flies, and about caring for the cage kindly without being trapped by it or taking it for the singer.
doha on body as a cage for breath
The cage has nine small gates, and the breath, a restless bird, sings a while and slips away.
Standing next to my father's hospital bed I felt his body was a cage and his breath was a singing bird that was preparing to leave.
doha on the river wearing down this body
The river near my village has eaten a little more of the bank every year, just like age has eaten my father's body.
river, body, wearing away
The river of years wears down the bank; this body, bank of the breath, is slowly carried away.
Compose a verse about this body that the river of time wears down grain by grain, a bank that crumbles slowly, which we should tend and strengthen while we can but cannot ever hold forever.
From a seed in the earth rises this body, a pearl of breath, precious and small, and back to the earth it goes.
When my daughter was born I called her my pearl and my seed of the future, and I touched her tiny hand and thought of how fragile all bodies are.
Write a doha about this body as a pearl formed in secret, fragile and precious beyond price, cared for as treasure, yet understood as part of a cycle that begins as a seed and ends as dust.
seed, pearl, body
doha on this body as a pearl, born of a seed
The influencers I follow spend hours on their looks, and last week one of them got sick and posted that she had never felt so frail.

Write a doha about the way we spend our days feeding, decorating, and worrying over this body, as if it were the whole of us, while forgetting it is only a lovely, delicate instrument that we borrowed.
why do we treat our body like it's everything
body is not everything
Adorn the frame, feed the frame, and then let the frame go; it is only a coat for the one who walks.
Watching a potter shape a pot of clay and then spotting a snake's shed skin by the wall, I felt how lightly we should hold our own bodies.
potter's clay, snake, body
doha on this body as potter's clay and a snake's shed skin
Compose a doha about this body as a clay vessel fashioned by the potter, sweet to hold and easily broken, and the snake that sheds its skin the way the soul sheds this body when the time comes.
The potter shapes the clay vessel with love and the snake sheds its skin without grief; so this body is given and let go.
Write a verse about this body as an inn where the guest rests a night, cared for kindly by its keeper, but never to be owned or clung to because the morning always comes.
doha on body as an inn
After a week in a village inn, I packed my bag with a calm I wish I could carry into the day I leave my own body.
An inn of breath for a single night; tend it gently, for the traveller leaves at dawn.
body, inn, brief stay
moneylender, body, debt
The moneylender keeps a ledger of every breath, and this body, borrowed flesh, is repaid at last.
My neighbour kept saying he owed everything to the moneylender, and I realised that I too owe this body back to someone.
doha on a moneylender coming for this body
Write a verse about the moneylender who comes calling when the breaths are spent, and this body that has to be handed back without argument, having been only a loan of flesh for a few years.
